Written for Mr. Xunzhi at the monk's lodge in Huqiu on the winter day of the reign of the reigning emperor, Ding Yunpeng", with the seal of "Yunpeng" in vermilion and the seal of "Nan Yu" in vermilion. Inscriptions of "Three Heavenly Sons of Foreign Ministers" in white, "Shen Shuyong's seal" in white, and "Rhyme first examination" in vermilion. The year is the fortieth year of Wanli (1612).　　The picture depicts the famous Tang Dynasty scholar Lu Tong tea scene, is Ding Yunpeng late creation of fine brush painting. Lu Tong (about 796-835), a native of Jiyuan, was originally from Fangyang (now Zhuozhou, Hebei), and lived in seclusion on Shaomuro Mountain in his early years, calling himself Yuchuanzi, and later moved to Luoyang. He was a good poet and writer, and once wrote a poem called "Moon Eclipses" to stab the current affairs, which was praised by Han Yu. He was a good tea drinker and composed the "Tea Song" with many curious and alarming lines. On the picture, Lu Tong is dressed in casual clothes, wearing a turban and holding a feather fan, sitting cross-legged on a green stone in front of a banana, with strange rocks and green bamboo behind him and two servants waiting for him. Lu Tong stared at the tea stove on the fire, and his full concentration was delicately portrayed.
